components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Red pill CTA with hard offset shadow and press-down active state.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #d63a30; color: #fff; font-weight: 800; font-size: 16px; padding: 12px 22px; border-radius: 999px; box-shadow: 0 4px 0 #b0332b; transition: transform .1s; border: none; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(3px); box-shadow: none; }

components.name: Gold Button
components.description: Gold pill CTA reserved for the Grand Tour call to action.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn ds-btn-gold">🎒 Take the Grand Tour</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-gold { background: #f4b942; color: #2b2118; font-weight: 800; font-size: 16px; padding: 12px 22px; border-radius: 999px; box-shadow: 0 4px 0 #c48f1f; transition: transform .1s; border: none; } .ds-btn-gold:active { transform: translateY(3px); box-shadow: none; }

components.name: Category Chip
components.description: Filter chip; grayscale-dimmed when off, full color and text-contrast-aware when selected.
components.css: .ds-chip { border-radius: 999px; padding: 6px 12px; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 800; border: none; transition: filter .15s, transform .1s; filter: grayscale(1) opacity(.55); } .ds-chip-on { filter: none; } .ds-chip:hover { transform: scale(1.05); }

components.description: Landing-page fact card; rotates and lifts on hover.

narrative.overview: Middle Kingdom Explorer reads like an illustrated children's atlas rebuilt for adults: warm cream paper, thick candy-colored ink, and chunky solid-offset shadows that make every card feel like a physical panel sitting slightly off the page. The system is playful and tactile without going childish -- body copy stays plain and factual, while the chrome around it (buttons, chips, badges, the timeline itself) carries all the personality. Nothing in the shipped UI uses blur-based drop shadows, gradients-as-depth, or a muted archive palette; depth and hierarchy come entirely from flat color, solid hard-offset shadows, and pill/rounded geometry. Emoji glyphs are used throughout as the icon system -- a native, load-bearing device of this world's illustrated-atlas identity, not a placeholder.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream paper background throughout; never pure white as a page surface
Hard, solid (non-blurred) offset shadows on cards, buttons, and floating UI chrome
Fredoka for all display/heading text, Nunito for everything read at length
Pill-shaped (999px) buttons, chips, and badges; softly rounded (12-18px) cards and panels
Category color is a first-class UI signal carried consistently across chips, timeline, map, badges

rules.name: The One Category, One Color Rule
rules.body: A category's color is identical everywhere it appears -- chip, timeline band, map pin, detail badge. Never reassign a category color contextually.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Fredoka is reserved for headings, labels, and UI chrome; Nunito is reserved for anything meant to be read as a sentence.

rules.name: The Press-Down Rule
rules.body: Every hard-offset button collapses its shadow and translates down on :active, simulating a physical button press.

dos: Do use hard, zero-blur, solid-color offset shadows for anything at resting elevation; reserve blurred shadows for true modal/overlay layers only.
Do use pill radius (999px) for every interactive/tag element and 12-18px rounding for every container surface.
Do use Fredoka for headings/labels and Nunito for body copy; never mix within one text node.
Do keep one category to one color mapping consistent across chips, timeline bands, map pins, and badges.
Do use emoji glyphs as the icon system -- they are this world's native iconography.
donts: Don't introduce blurred ambient drop shadows on resting cards or buttons -- it would erase the comic-panel identity that hard offsets establish.
Don't use pure white as a full-page background; the page surface is always the warm paper cream.
Don't introduce a new accent color for a UI element that already maps to a category color.
Don't use sharp (0px) corners or outline-only borders for surface separation; this system defines depth with color and shadow, not strokes.
